title: Interactive Shell Spawned By A Web Service Process
detection_hypothesis: If server-side content is used to execute commands, the resulting shell process will retain the web service worker as its parent image.

field_semantics.ParentImage: Absolute path of the executable that created the process.
field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.

collection_prerequisites: An execve audit rule or equivalent process telemetry agent is deployed.
Audit rules are not limited to a narrow allowlist of binaries.
expected_collection_gaps: Containers without a shared audit namespace may not report execve records.
Audit backlog limits can drop records under load.
normalization_assumptions: Image is the absolute executable path and CommandLine is the joined argument vector.
ParentImage identifies the parent executable path.
ingestion_differences: auditd argument vectors may be hex-encoded before normalization.
Some agents report the argv array instead of a joined string.
retention_considerations: Execve telemetry is high volume; 30 to 60 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Very low; each match warrants immediate triage.
false_positive_strategy: The benign population is tiny and always uses the same command line. Tune on the exact command line of the deployment hook and require that it disappears outside release windows.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the specific health check command line only. Never exclude the web worker parent, which would remove the only reliable web shell signal available from process telemetry.
test_strategy: Positive cases pair two different web parents with two different shells. Negative cases keep the web parent with a non-shell child and place a shell under an ordinary parent.

attack_techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
